questions.question: 1. Which of the following traversals in trees is equivalent to topological sort ?

explanations.a: Correct. In Topological Sort, the nodes are sorted such that the parent of a particular node always comes before the node in the ordering. In Pre-Order Traversal the parent node is traversed first then childs from left to right.
explanations.b: Incorrect. In Post-Order Traversal the childs are traversed from left to right than the parent node.
explanations.c: Incorrect. In In-order Transversal first the order is left child, parent, right child.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Pre-Order Traversal is equivalent to topological sort in trees.

questions.question:
2. Which of the following are applications of topological Sorting?
Finding prerequisite of a task
Finding Deadlock in an Operating System
Finding Cycle in a graph

explanations.a: Incorrect. While finding prerequisites is an application, there are other applications as well.
explanations.b: Incorrect. While finding deadlocks and cycles are applications, finding prerequisites is also an application.
explanations.c: Correct. 1. Topological Sort can be used to determine which task needs to be finished first (parent node) before a task (child node) can be started. 2. While using threads in the Operating System, sometimes the program gets stuck in a deadlock as the commands waiting become dependent on each other. It creates a cycle of commands. Topological Sort can be used to detect cycles in a graph as if we try to sort it the nodes appear again and again in the sequence. 3. Topological Sort can be used to detect cycles in a graph as if we try to sort it the nodes appear again and again in the sequence.
explanations.d: Incorrect. All three options are valid applications of topological sorting.

questions.question: 3. What is the most efficient Time Complexity of Topological Sorting?( N= number of vertices , E = number of edges)

explanations.a: Correct. The most efficient time complexity of Topological Sorting is O(N+E), where N is the number of vertices and E is the number of edges.
explanations.b: Incorrect. O(N) would only account for visiting vertices without processing edges.
explanations.c: Incorrect. O(V) is the same as O(N) and doesn't account for edge processing.
explanations.d: Incorrect. O(V*E) would be much slower than the actual complexity of topological sorting.

questions.question: 4. The topological sort of Directed Acyclic graph is always unique.

explanations.a: Correct. The topological sort of a graph can be unique if we assume the graph as a single linked list and we can have multiple topological sort order if we consider a graph as a complete binary tree.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The topological sort of a Directed Acyclic Graph is not always unique; it depends on the structure of the graph.
